cards.confidenceNote: Truce terms from Reuters (Beijing dateline) carried by gCaptain; rare earths are not named in the text. Trump's remarks from Euronews; China's position from earlier MFA statements via AP.
cards.title: China extends US trade truce; Trump expects Putin-Xi meeting
cards.summary: China extended its trade truce with the US by two months on 9 November: a 24% tariff stays suspended, and critical-mineral export waivers and port-fee suspensions run to 10 January 2027. Trump says he expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November.
cards.body:
The 10 November cliff in US-China trade passed quietly. On 9 November China's state council, commerce ministry and transport ministry announced that every measure suspended after September's Washington summit stays suspended for two more months (Reuters, Beijing). A 24% additional tariff on US goods remains off for two months from 10 November, though a 10% tariff stays. Export-control waivers for 'certain critical minerals and related technologies' run to 10 January 2027, as do the suspension of measures against 11 US firms on China's unreliable-entity list and 16 on its export-control list, the suspension of special port fees on US-linked ships, and sanctions on five US units of Hanwha Ocean. The Reuters text does not name rare earths, and whether these waivers cover them is not confirmed.

Beijing framed the move as implementing 'the outcomes and consensus' of the Washington meeting. It also warned that it is watching US plans to replace tariffs struck down by the courts with Section 301 tariffs, and will 'adjust relevant countermeasures' if needed. The truce now ends on 10 January, giving both sides a new deadline after APEC.

The summit is the next test. Trump said on 8 November he expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November (Euronews). China's foreign ministry has said only that it is 'in communication with relevant parties' about a three-leader meeting. Neither government has published an agenda. A three-way meeting would be the first of its kind and would come while Washington is trying to close both the Iran war and a Ukraine deal; Euronews reports Iran is expected on the agenda.

Two frictions could intrude. Nvidia's board is investigating chief executive Jensen Huang over an affair with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China, and Trump said the FBI is investigating and that Xi may raise the case; the board has not confirmed details beyond press reports. And Lithuania's president confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's office in Vilnius, which Beijing has demanded since 2021, while Chinese diplomats are expected in the country this week.

What to watch: confirmation of a Shenzhen meeting and its format; whether any purchase or tariff package is signed there; China's response to the Huang case; and whether the January deadline is extended again or becomes leverage.

cards.confidenceNote: French attribution from France 24 (AFP) and NPR; minister and prosecutor statements on record. Mildenhall from Reuters via The Guardian and Al Jazeera, resting on the WSJ and one US official.
cards.title: France blames Iran's Guard for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges
cards.summary: France blamed the Revolutionary Guard's Shahid Kaveh unit for October cyberattacks that raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets. Prosecutors seek warrants for two officials; France will summon Iran's ambassador and seek EU sanctions. The US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat.
cards.body:
France has made the first government attribution of a large-scale Iranian cyber sabotage campaign on European soil. Foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the Revolutionary Guard was behind attacks on 11-12 October that raised the temperature of refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, calling it the first operation of its kind against France (France 24, citing AFP; NPR). Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau opened an investigation into the Guard's cyber unit Shahid Kaveh and requested international arrest warrants for two of its officials. Barrot said France 'rules nothing out', will summon Iran's ambassador and will seek sanctions at EU level. France 24 reports similar suspected attacks on 2 November hit stores in at least nine other European countries, which have not been named or attributed.

The pattern matches one already on the board. At the end of October Pentagon officials told Reuters they were treating freezer failures at US military commissaries as a suspected hack, without naming an attacker. France's attribution does not mention those incidents, and the board does not link them.

The same day brought a physical security signal. The US moved two refuelling tankers from RAF Mildenhall to Germany on 9 November and later moved others, after a threat from Iran, the Wall Street Journal reported (via Reuters in The Guardian and Al Jazeera). A US official said Mildenhall and nearby Lakenheath were raised to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest protection level, used when intelligence suggests an attack is likely. The nature of the threat is still being assessed. It is the second British base the US has vacated, after bombers left RAF Fairford in September following arrests on suspicion of helping Iranian intelligence; Britain's prime minister has said that activity was likely coordinated in Iran.

Taken together, Iran's response to the war is reaching Europe through deniable channels: cyber sabotage of civilian systems and threats to bases used against it. The French case is a government attribution with a criminal investigation behind it. The Mildenhall case rests on anonymous officials.

What to watch: whether France summons the ambassador and the EU lists anyone; whether the nine other countries attribute their incidents; any explanation of the Mildenhall threat; and whether US commissary investigators name an attacker.

cards.confidenceNote: Trump's remarks from AFP and AP via Arab News and from Euronews; Huda from Euronews (US account); Iron Gate from The New Arab; Guard tanker claims are its own, unconfirmed by Reuters.
cards.title: Trump calls further Iran strikes unlikely as US enforces blockade
cards.summary: Trump said on 9 November that the war is 'militarily effectively over' and further US strikes are 'quite unlikely'. US aircraft disabled the cargo ship Huda running the blockade east of Khor Fakkan; 22 crew were rescued. CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate to cut land routes into Iran.
cards.body:
After two strike days on Iranian territory in a week (2 and 6 November), Trump changed his tone. After meeting Qatar's prime minister and Vice President Vance at the White House, he said the war is 'militarily effectively over' and new strikes are 'quite unlikely', while saying the US remains 'locked and loaded' (Arab News, citing AFP and AP). A day earlier he told reporters the US had 'won' and that renewed fighting was 'highly unlikely', but tied that to Iran signing 'a very strong agreement'. He said three US carriers remain in the region and named power plants and bridges as possible targets (Euronews).

The military pressure has moved to the blockade. Late on 7 November US aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the St Kitts-flagged cargo ship Huda about 18 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan, after its crew ignored repeated warnings to stop trying to run the blockade. UAE forces rescued 22 crew; no one was killed (Euronews, citing CENTCOM and UKMTO accounts). CENTCOM says it has redirected 147 vessels and disabled five merchant ships since July. On 8 November it set up Task Force Iron Gate, a small team charged with stopping weapons, dual-use goods and sanctioned materials crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian (The New Arab).

Iran's side of the record is unconfirmed. The Guard said two tankers hit mines and caught fire on an 'unauthorised' route, and Fars reported a third; Reuters could not confirm any of them, and Iranian state television suggested the blasts were not US attacks (Reuters via gCaptain). No ship has been named. A Guard spokesman said on 7 November that the range restriction on Iran's ballistic missiles 'has been lifted', without saying whether Iran has longer-range missiles than the 2,000 km it has declared.

The sea lane itself remains contested. No verified daily transit count is available; Lloyd's List Intelligence's weekly monitor shows non-Iranian transits falling in late October.

What to watch: whether Trump's restraint holds if talks stall; further blockade interceptions and any Iranian response at sea; confirmation of a ship from the Guard's mine claims; and whether Iron Gate produces seizures on land routes.

cards.confidenceNote: Trump and Rubio statements on record (Arab News, Euronews); Rezaei's statement via AFP. Qatar plan terms still rest on anonymous officials quoted by Reuters on 7 November.
cards.title: Qatar's prime minister takes Iran mediation to the White House
cards.summary: Qatar's prime minister met Trump and Vance on 9 November to discuss advancing US-Iran talks; no Iranian officials took part. Rubio reported no progress. Iran's Rezaei told Washington to stop 'manufacturing fake news' about talks and accept Iran's seven conditions.
cards.body:
Qatar carried its mediation to Washington. Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Trump and Vice President Vance at the White House on 9 November to discuss ways to advance talks with Iran (Arab News, citing AFP and AP). No Iranian participation was reported. Afterwards Trump said the war was effectively over militarily and spoke of positive momentum toward a deal. Secretary of State Rubio was more cautious: he reported no progress and no breakthrough in sight, and no US negotiating delegation is scheduled (Euronews).

Tehran's public answer was hostile. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, told the US to stop 'manufacturing fake news' about negotiations and to accept Iran's seven conditions. Iran's foreign ministry says sanctions and the naval blockade must end before talks, and that its own proposal to reopen Hormuz for two days 'remains on the table'.

The plan on the table has not changed since regional officials described it to Reuters on 7 November: on day one the US would lift its blockade and release some frozen funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors to bombed sites; on day two Iran would reopen the Strait under an arrangement with Oman that the US has not approved. Iran's conditions for nuclear talks include lifting the blockade and sanctions, unfreezing assets, war-damage compensation and an end to hostilities, including in Lebanon. The sequencing gap remains: Washington wants inspections and a reopening, Tehran wants the blockade lifted first.

The broader context is shifting. Trump faces a Congress controlled by Democrats after the midterms, and a poll cited by Arab News shows most Americans put prices ahead of war aims. Egypt's foreign minister says both sides want to negotiate. Iraq is being pressed by Washington to close border crossings with Iran.

What to watch: whether a US delegation meets Iranian officials, directly or through Qatar; any Iranian written response to the bridge plan; whether the US softens on the Iran-Oman routing; and whether France's cyber attribution complicates European support for a deal.

cards.confidenceNote: Mandate from The Guardian and the NYT (7 Nov); recommendation count and unity-government exchange from Ynet via research return (not a directory outlet), stated as reported.
cards.title: Herzog asks Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
cards.summary: President Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on 7 November after more lawmakers recommended him than Netanyahu. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister and has called for a unity government; Eisenkot's camp rejects it in its current form.
cards.body:
Israel's post-election deadlock has its first formal step. President Isaac Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff who leads the opposition camp, the mandate to form a government on 7 November, after more Knesset members recommended him than Netanyahu (The Guardian; New York Times). Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to assemble a majority. The election on 27 October gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 of 120 seats, Eisenkot's camp 48 and Arab-majority parties a record 19, so no bloc holds 61 without crossing lines its members have drawn.

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister with full authority over military operations, including decisions on Iran. He has called for a national unity government; Eisenkot's side says it will not join one in its current form and wants Likud to drop its far-right partners, according to Israeli reporting. Herzog said the next government must advance the US 20-point Gaza plan through the Board of Peace, and Trump publicly told Netanyahu to stop obstructing it. Israel's Shin Bet reportedly found no evidence of foreign interference in the election, after Netanyahu's camp had alleged fraud.

For the Iran war, the change matters through command authority. Israeli reporting last week said Netanyahu and the Mossad chief had planned an operation against Iran on the eve of the election that was halted after the US was told; that report is disputed. A caretaker government can still act, but a transition to an Eisenkot-led coalition would put a former chief of staff who has been critical of open-ended operations in charge of the Iran and Lebanon files.

In Lebanon, Israeli drone strikes continue in the south; Lebanon's health ministry reported one person killed on 4 November in Qabrikha, and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam warned against Lebanon being drawn into a renewed US-Iran war.

What to watch: whether Eisenkot can win over ultra-Orthodox or Arab-backed support; any unity-government talks; caretaker decisions on Iran or Lebanon during the mandate; and the Gaza plan's progress.

cards.confidenceNote: Each strand is sourced on its own card; this card synthesises. US proposal details from The Guardian; Trump's Iran remarks from Arab News (AFP/AP).
cards.title: US pivots to talks on Iran and Ukraine as pressure shifts
cards.summary: Trump called the Iran war effectively over while the blockade tightened, and US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks opened in Abu Dhabi with a wider European agenda. China rolled over its trade truce, and Trump expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC. France blamed Iran for cyber sabotage in Europe.
cards.body:
Washington spent the weekend turning from force to bargaining on two fronts at once. On Iran, Trump said after meeting Qatar's prime minister that the war is militarily 'effectively over' and new strikes are unlikely, but the blockade is being enforced harder: US aircraft disabled a ship running it off Khor Fakkan, and a new task force targets land routes. Talks have not moved, by Rubio's account, and Iran repeats its conditions.

On Ukraine, the three delegations met in Abu Dhabi on 10 November for the first time since February. US officials describe a deal reaching well beyond Ukraine: a 'long-term security architecture' between Russia and Europe, a possible revival of the NATO-Russia Council, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Kyiv (The Guardian). Europe is in Abu Dhabi but outside the core format; France says European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire, and the Kremlin rejects any European role.

The great-power layer is calmer than it looked a week ago. China rolled over every suspended trade measure to 10 January, defusing the 10 November cliff, and Trump says he expects a three-way meeting with Putin and Xi at APEC on 18-19 November.

The alliance picture carries the main risk. Allies are being asked to accept a US-designed security settlement for Europe while the US floats sanctions relief for Russia, and Europe's leaders have said publicly they will not implement terms made without them. At the same time Iran's war is reaching European territory through deniable means: France has attributed cyber sabotage to the Revolutionary Guard, and the US moved aircraft out of a second British base over an Iranian threat.

The risk score holds at 65. Kinetic activity continues at a high level (Houthi strikes on Riyadh, Russian strikes on power plants, a disabled blockade runner) but no new direct US strike on Iran followed the president's remarks. No ally has broken with Washington on an operational commitment; the disagreements are public and the coordination continues.

What to watch: the first readouts from Abu Dhabi; any sanctions-relief step for Russia; Iran's answer to Qatar; and whether Shenzhen produces a three-leader meeting.

cards.confidenceNote: Talks opening from Arab News (AFP) and Kyiv Independent; US proposal from The Guardian; ZNPP from the IAEA via Kyiv Independent; Trypillia from Centrenergo via Kyiv Independent.
cards.title: Russia and Ukraine open first talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi
cards.summary: Russian and Ukrainian delegations met with US envoys in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first such talks since February. US officials want a 'final end' and a Russia-Europe security framework. A drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, and Russia struck the Trypillia power plant near Kyiv.
cards.body:
The talks began on 10 November. Russian state media published a photograph of the two delegations sitting opposite each other with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the head of the table (Arab News, citing AFP). Ukraine's team is led by defence minister Rustem Umerov; Russia's by Vladimir Medinsky, and for the first time it includes Sergei Ryabkov, the diplomat who issued Moscow's 2021 ultimatum on NATO's footprint in eastern Europe. A senior Ukrainian official said Kyiv has no particular expectations. Ukraine's agenda is a cessation of hostilities, security guarantees and humanitarian steps, including a possible energy and maritime ceasefire.

The US agenda is wider. Administration officials told The Guardian they seek a 'final end' to the war and a 'long-term security architecture' between Russia and Europe, could revive the NATO-Russia Council, could lift sanctions on Russia as part of a deal, and have discussed guarantees for Ukraine 'very similar to NATO'. Trump has said Ukraine will end up 'a little bit different shape'. Russia still demands the rest of Donetsk.

Europe is present but outside the format. Officials from Germany, France, Britain, Italy, NATO and the EU met Ukraine's delegation and US negotiators separately (Kyiv Independent; The Guardian). France's foreign minister said Europeans would be 'in the meeting room' and that European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire; the Kremlin said there is no role for Europeans. The EU's Kallas said Europe already has a security architecture that Russia is not respecting.

The war continued around the table. The IAEA said a drone killed a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on 9 November, a day after it lost its only external power line for about 10 hours and ran on diesel generators; a second drone killed a worker at the nearby thermal plant. Russian forces struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv, which its operator says may have 'extremely serious' consequences. Bulgaria confirmed six bodies aboard the tanker Wine Trader, hit by drones off Romania on 15 October.

What to watch: readouts from the second day; any agreed energy or maritime ceasefire; whether sanctions relief is offered publicly; whether Europeans meet Russia's delegation; and the nuclear plant's power line.

iran_lead.title: Trump calls Iran war 'effectively over' as US enforces blockade
iran_lead.summary: Trump said on 9 November, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, that the war is 'militarily effectively over' and further strikes are 'quite unlikely'. Rubio reported no progress in talks. US aircraft disabled a cargo ship running the blockade off Khor Fakkan, and the US moved tankers out of a British base over an Iranian threat.
facts: 9 November: Trump called the war 'militarily effectively over' and new strikes 'quite unlikely', after meeting Qatar's prime minister and Vance (Arab News, citing AFP and AP).
Rubio reported no progress in talks; Iran's Rezaei told the US to accept Iran's seven conditions (Euronews; Arab News).
7 November: US aircraft disabled the cargo ship Huda east of Khor Fakkan for running the blockade; 22 crew rescued, no deaths (Euronews).
8 November: CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate to stop goods reaching Iran over land and the Caspian (The New Arab).
9 November: the US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat; FPCON Charlie at two bases (The Guardian, citing Reuters and the WSJ).
9 November: France blamed the Revolutionary Guard for supermarket cyberattacks and will seek EU sanctions (France 24; NPR).
iran_lead.changed: Washington's message shifted from strikes to economic pressure: Trump now calls more strikes unlikely, while the blockade is enforced at sea and a new task force targets land routes. Talks have not moved, by Rubio's account. Iran's confrontation with the West widened beyond the Gulf, with France attributing cyber sabotage to the Guard and the US moving aircraft from a British base over an Iranian threat. The Guard again claims tankers hit mines; none is confirmed.
iran_lead.watch: Whether Iran answers Qatar or a US delegation joins talks; any further US strike despite Trump's remarks; more blockade interceptions; France's response and any EU listing; the threat behind the Mildenhall move; confirmation of the Guard's tanker claims.

brics_lead.title: China extends US trade truce as Trump eyes three-leader meeting
brics_lead.summary: China extended its trade truce with the US by two months, keeping a 24% tariff suspended and critical-mineral export waivers in place to 10 January. Trump says he expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November. France blamed Iran's Guard for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges.
brics_lead.changed: The economic cliff of 10 November passed without a fight: Beijing rolled over every suspended measure for two months, citing the Washington summit. The three-leader meeting moved from Chinese hints to Trump saying he expects it. In Europe, Iran joined Russia as a named source of cyber sabotage, and US forces moved aircraft out of a British base. Lithuania opened talks on renaming Taiwan's office, a reversal of its 2021 stance.
brics_lead.watch: Whether the White House or Beijing confirms a Shenzhen meeting with Putin; APEC on 18-19 November; the Quad summit in Manila; China's response to the Nvidia spy case; Lithuania's talks with Chinese diplomats; North Korean launches.

lenses.label: Bilateral US-China
lenses.oneline: China extended the truce two months to 10 January, including critical-mineral waivers; Trump expects to meet Xi and Putin at APEC.

lenses.label: BRICS bloc
lenses.oneline: No material bloc development in the window.

lenses.label: CRINK
lenses.oneline: Trump expects a three-way meeting with Putin and Xi in Shenzhen; China says only that talks are under way.

lenses.label: Allies Cohesion
lenses.oneline: Europeans met delegations outside the Abu Dhabi talks; France blamed Iran for cyber sabotage; the US moved aircraft from RAF Mildenhall.

facts: 4 November: several missiles fired from Sondok toward the Sea of Japan, per South Korea's military (Al Jazeera).
Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's Binance attribution a provocation and ruled out talks with the US (Al Jazeera).
3 November: Peskov said a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting should be finalised within days for later in November; China did not mention Trump (The Moscow Times).
3 November: Taiwan reported 49 sorties in 24 hours, the year's highest, with the Liaoning group in the western Pacific (SCMP).
3 November: Belousov in Beijing called military ties unprecedented (Kyiv Post).
3 November: Poland sent forces and counter-terrorism police to the Kaliningrad border; Norway added NASAMS sensors at Kirkenes (The Moscow Times; Kyiv Post; Kyiv Independent).

ukraine_lead.title: Russia and Ukraine open US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
ukraine_lead.summary: Russian and Ukrainian delegations sat down with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first such talks in nine months. US officials say they want a 'final end' and a new Russia-Europe security architecture. A drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, the IAEA said.
facts: 10 November: talks opened with the delegations facing each other and US envoys at the head of the table; Medinsky leads Russia, Umerov Ukraine (Arab News, citing AFP; Kyiv Independent).
US officials floated a revived NATO-Russia Council, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine (The Guardian).
European officials met Ukraine and US negotiators outside the three-way format; the Kremlin rejects a European role (Kyiv Independent; The Moscow Times).
9 November: the IAEA said a drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, which lost its only external line for about 10 hours on 8 November (Kyiv Independent).
9 November: Russia struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv (Kyiv Independent).
Bulgaria confirmed six bodies aboard the tanker Wine Trader, hit by drones off Romania on 15 October (Euromaidan Press).
ukraine_lead.changed: The three sides are in one room for the first time since February, and the US agenda is wider than Ukraine: officials describe a security architecture for Russia and Europe and say sanctions relief could be part of a deal. Europe is present in Abu Dhabi but outside the core format, and France says European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire. Russia kept striking power plants before the talks.
ukraine_lead.watch: Whether the talks produce any ceasefire terms, including energy or maritime; whether a European joins a session with Russia; US moves on sanctions relief; another mass missile strike; the Zaporizhzhia plant's power supply.
